after: ## Why HL-only content clusters where it does
alt: Five theme panels list sub-topics A.1 to E.5. Five are HL only: A.4 rigid body mechanics, A.5 Galilean and special relativity, B.4 thermodynamics, D.4 induction and E.2 quantum physics.
caption: HL-only content clusters where the core models become more abstract.

after: ## Theme E -- Nuclear and quantum physics (23 hours SL / 39 hours HL)
alt: Paired bars of recommended hours: Theme A 27 SL and 42 HL, Theme B 24 and 32, Theme C 17 and 29, Theme D 19 and 38, Theme E 23 and 39. Total teaching time is 150 hours at SL and 240 at HL, including a 40-hour or 60-hour experimental programme.
caption: Theme A is the largest at both levels; Theme D gains the most hours at HL.

alt: The 40-hour SL or 60-hour HL experimental programme is made up of practical work, a collaborative sciences project shared with other group 4 subjects and an internally assessed scientific investigation. It builds three skills, designing a fair test, reducing uncertainty and interpreting unfamiliar data, which are examined in the written papers and the internal assessment.
caption: The practical skills are examined twice: in the papers and in the investigation.

after: ## Command terms across the five themes
alt: Four steps of rising demand: state or define asks for a precise recalled fact; describe for an account of a pattern or process without explanation; explain for a reasoned account of why, often backed by a named law; evaluate or discuss for weighing a model, method or conclusion, including limitations. A warning notes that explain needs the physical reasoning behind a formula, not just the calculation.
caption: Each command term asks for more than the one below it.
